plan.name: Resolve Python contract implementations consistently
plan.summary: Make trusted-contract implementation resolution agree on Python 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14: a class or named Python method must resolve from methods actually declared in that class's source, so generated methods and annotation helpers cannot qualify merely because their compiled qualified names look class-owned. Preserve the existing refusals for generated-only dataclasses, including pstats.StatsProfile, and preserve real methods, receiver and globals checks, source and wheel RECORD attribution, call counts and exception observation; receipts must explain the observed unresolved implementation or missing calls without choosing a reason by Python version. Both tests named in #479 must pass on all three versions with every existing refusal and reason preserved, and the remaining Python tests in internal/verify and internal/verify/pythongate must pass on 3.14; the new focused acceptance file exercises the resolution defect under the sandbox's 3.13 without running those whole suites. Update SPEC.md and docs/python.md to name the three supported versions, retain the separately pinned 3.13 execution image, and explain source-based method ownership with citations to D-0216, D-0234, D-0241 and D-0304. The merger must record the decision refining method-ownership resolution and extending documented support to 3.14, since the plumbing build cannot write decisions/.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationResolutionRefusesGeneratedOnlyClasses
tests.says: Generated-only classes and generated methods named on their class stay unresolved even with class-qualified compiled names; the report keeps their contracts untested and explains the unresolved implementation, including the native dataclass and pstats.StatsProfile refusal cases.

tests.name: TestPythonApplicationResolutionCountsOnlyDeclaredMethods
tests.says: A class with both declared and generated methods resolves to its declared implementation: calling only a generated helper leaves its contract untested for missing calls, while real declared methods still support contracts with the bound source and wheel identity.
